goals.summary: Fix imports in the V1 Hypothesis plugin under Pydantic V2

facets.summary: In Pydantic V2, importing top-level `pydantic`, `pydantic.color`, and `pydantic.types` in `pydantic/v1/_hypothesis_plugin.py` caused `AttributeError` at import time because those point to V2 modules lacking V1-specific attributes like `color.r_rgba` and `types.ConstrainedNumberMeta`.
Imports `pydantic.v1 as pydantic`, relying on `pydantic.v1` exposing `color` and `types` directly and avoiding unaliased submodule imports that overwrite top-level bindings.
Reproduced CI test failures when `pydantic.generics` was loaded, and confirmed regression tests fail if original imports are restored.
Author reports 53 related tests pass on Python 3.13, tests filter the known Hypothesis deprecation warning, and Ruff lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.

candidates.whyInspect: Shows the implementation change replacing unaliased top-level pydantic and submodule imports with aliased pydantic.v1.
candidates.reviewQuestion: Does aliasing pydantic.v1 as pydantic ensure that all downstream color and types attribute lookups inside the module resolve to V1 structures without shadowing?
candidates.uncertainty: Surrounding plugin code using pydantic.color and pydantic.types is not fully visible in this diff slice.

candidates.whyInspect: Contains regression tests asserting that the V1 hypothesis plugin imports cleanly under V2 and registers expected strategies.
candidates.reviewQuestion: Do the regression tests adequately exercise the previously failing attribute lookups from color and types during strategy registration?
candidates.uncertainty: Tests only evaluate StrictBool and conint; coverage for color or other constrained types is not directly exercised in this test.

candidates.whyInspect: Shows the base version imports that previously caused AttributeError under V2.
candidates.reviewQuestion: Which exact imports were removed and could any external code rely on them being imported in this namespace?
candidates.uncertainty: Internal plugin module, typically not imported directly by end users.

context.text: `pydantic/v1/_hypothesis_plugin.py` ships with Pydantic V2
But it imported the top-level names `pydantic`, `pydantic.color` and `pydantic.types`
Under V2, those names point to the V2 modules
So the V1-only names that the module reads from them (`color.r_rgba`, `types.ConstrainedNumberMeta`, `types._DEFINED_TYPES`) raised `AttributeError` at import time
The plugin could not be imported at all
This change points the import at the V1 namespace:
import pydantic
import pydantic.color
import pydantic.types
+import pydantic.v1 as pydantic
The package `pydantic.v1` already exposes `color` and `types` as attributes
So one aliased import is enough
A separate `import pydantic.v1.color` is not needed
That form would also break: `import a.b.c` without `as` binds the top-level name `pydantic` again and overwrites the alias
Reproduced both CI test failures with `pydantic.generics` already loaded
The tests now filter only the known Hypothesis `GenericModel` deprecation warning
53 related tests passed locally on Python 3.13
Restoring the original imports still makes both regression tests fail

evidenceIndex.summary:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

## Change Summary

`pydantic/v1/_hypothesis_plugin.py` ships with Pydantic V2. But it imported the top-level names `pydantic`, `pydantic.color` and `pydantic.types`. Under V2, those names point to the V2 modules. So the V1-only names that the module reads from them (`color.r_rgba`, `types.ConstrainedNumberMeta`, `types._DEFINED_TYPES`) raised `AttributeError` at import time. The plugin could not be imported at all.

This change points the import at the V1 namespace:

    -import pydantic.color
    -import pydantic.types
    +import pydantic.v1 as pyd
